- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; adjust downward bias in high-activity periods.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; apply a 1–2 day smoothing or lead correction for near-term price expectations.
- After a price spike, model overestimates subsequent values (overshoot), then underestimates the true mean; apply a “cool-down” correction after peak, reducing forecast by 5–10% for 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–15% to align with historical mean reversion behavior.
- In low-volatility periods (e.g., 2022–2023 winter), model overestimates downward trends; apply a “floor” correction to prevent excessive downward drift.
- Forecast often fails to capture seasonal or policy-driven price shifts (e.g., ETS auction cycles); add a “policy lag” buffer of +2–5% for regulatory-driven price surges.
